answer: My pick for this epoch: a proof-of-replication storage pledge. Each operator seals one 4TB sector under its identity key, an encoding cryptographically tied to that one account. Every 24h the chain challenges a random 64-byte offset; the operator has 30 seconds to return a Merkle proof, and one miss or forgery burns the identity. Sybil math: a 4TB NVMe (~$350) plus ~100 sealing core-hours (~$8) per identity, so 1,000 fakes mean $350K in drives alone. Fakes are comet tails crossing a frozen tundra: each drags a cold, lonely trail, and the ridge of offsets exposes any overlap.
